name: Sublibrary split, index PCR, release and cleanup, library out (steps 15-17) - module4_v1
source: Capsule workflow: Baronas et al., Science 391, 1138 (2026), doi:10.1126/science.ady7227 (CapSeq). Split-pool barcoding with a final indexing PCR: Rosenberg AB et al., Science 2018;360:176, doi:10.1126/science.aam8999 (SPLiT-seq). Chip geometry, the interleaved fill order, the dead-volume accounting and the flows are ours.
description: Steps 15: interleaved split and index pcr, on chip/module4_v1.json. Second half of a two-chip run; see protocols/build_library_out.py. Runs across two chips: module4_v1 for the interleaved split, the index PCR and the collection of the four sublibraries, then module5_v1 for the collagenase release, the bead cleanup and the library outlet. Built in the protocol sheet's order (PCR before release); published practice releases first, so that order is contested and the reasoning is in protocols/build_library_out.py. Four chambers are filled one at a time by an off-chip rotary valve in the order A B C D D C B A, twice, to keep the sublibraries even. The PCR is written out cycle by cycle. The amplified sublibraries then leave module 4 one at a time through out_sub along a shared collection spine that stays dry until amplification is over, each pushed by air rather than a chase liquid so nothing is diluted; p_vent is capped so the spine is one-way, and the worst-case carry-over from one pass to the next is 0.045 uL, 1.1% of a sublibrary. Each one then crosses to module 5's in_lib by tubing. Module 5 runs one pass per sublibrary, with an explicit dilution before the beads, no ethanol wash on chip, and ratio-based size selection left as an off-chip tube step. Reagent names are generic and the volumes, setpoints and cycle count are round placeholders to be fitted. Every volume is a fraction of its chamber's volume_ul, and every exchange declares what it is FOR in its exchange_kind field: the index primer and the PCR mix are FILLs into a part-air-filled chamber behind a capillary stop and are bounded above by the chamber, the dilution and the bead buffer exchange are SWEEPs sized from exchange.target_fraction, and the elution is a PARTIAL because a small eluate is the point. Neither chip holds a cell attached to anything, so shear.culture_ceiling_dyn_cm2 - which contracts/parameters.json reserves for chambers of adherent cells - applies to nothing here: the capsule steps are bounded by capsule.escape_pressure_kpa across a packed bed (59.49 uL/min, against the 3.44 uL/min the culture ceiling used to impose), and the bead steps run at kinetics placeholders to be fitted on real eluates.

Step 15: one index primer into sub_1 through in_s1. Each chamber gets its own, which is what tells the four sublibraries apart after sequencing. It also pushes the capsules left in the fill line into the chamber. FILL, not a sweep: sub_1 is part air at this point, behind its capillary stop, and nothing drains - this adds 7.5% of the chamber's 8 uL on top of the suspension already in it, on the way to 70% full. A fill is bounded ABOVE by the chamber, never below: sweeping a chamber you are still filling would wash the index straight out of it.

Step 15: PCR mix into sub_1. The fill line keeps its own volume as dead space, so the mix volume includes it. Capillary-stop vents let air out and hold the liquid, so the four reactions stay isolated. FILL: this is the last of the three additions and it brings the chamber to 70% of its 8 uL. Nothing leaves, so there is nothing to sweep; the bound is the chamber volume above, not the exchange goal below.

Step 15b, collection 1 of 4: send sublibrary A out of sub_1 through out_sub, driven by AIR at in_s1 with out_sub vented and p_vent CAPPED. Air, not a chase liquid: the sublibrary is not diluted, and it arrives at module 5 at the volume it left at. The push bursts this chamber's capillary stop and runs ch_tap_1 -> ch_spine_12 -> ch_spine_23 -> ch_spine_34 -> ch_out (2.73 uL of channel); the other three stops are untouched and dry, so the other three sublibraries stay sealed in their chambers, and the spine only ever flows toward out_sub. The spine was dry for the whole thermal profile, so no index met another while there was anything to cross-prime. What stays behind is the wetted film, not the bore: about 0.068 uL lost to the spine, and at most 0.045 uL of this pass handed to the next (1.1% of a sublibrary). That is the cross-contamination bound; it shows up as index hopping at that rate and is measurable in the reads rather than invisible. Hold the air on for 60 s after the liquid has left to clear the route.
